intro.line: Innistrad. A world of small stone villages, deep woods and a moon that is never quite safe to look at.
Long ago the vampire Sorin Markov made an angel, Avacyn, to keep the humans alive. For centuries she did.
For centuries my creation kept this world in balance. Now only her shadow remains.
Some priests speak in whispers of the Helvault, a silver prison of unpurged evils.
Avacyn locked the demon Griselbrand inside it, and the Helvault took her too. The angels are weak. The wolves are loud. The dead are walking.

finale.line: A golden helix streaked skyward from the Helvault. A thunderous explosion shattered the silver monolith and Avacyn emerged, free from her prison at last.
Avacyn emerged from the broken Helvault, but her freedom came at a price—him.
Griselbrand is out, and he is weakened, and Liliana Vess is waiting for him. She came to this world to kill a demon who held her contract. She does.
One down. Tell your angel she is welcome.
After the destruction of the Helvault, fearful mobs soon became fearless battalions.
The bells are ringing in Thraben again. I am not fool enough to think it lasts forever. Tonight, it is enough.

villainFinale.line: The Helvault stays shut. The moon stays red. Thraben's walls hold for one more winter, then they do not.
"Oh mighty Griselbrand, Scourge of the Heedless World, gladly I consume myself for thee!"
Let the silver hold her. I have more patience than your angel, and far more worshippers.

battles.title: The Hunter's Moon
battles.blurb: You arrive on a muddy road outside a Gavony village at dusk. Thalia, a knight-cathar of the Church of Avacyn, is holding the gate with a handful of militia. In the woods, the villagers who did not come home are changing shape.

cards.name: Kruin Outlaw // Terror of Kruin Pass

scene.line: As long as we can utter a prayer or lift a weapon, we have the power to fight back.
Transform: some cards have two faces. Werewolves are human by day, and turn over into wolves at night, when a turn passes with no spells cast. Cast something every turn and keep them human.

villainScene.line: When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.
Hey lads, the moon's rising. All the better to watch him beg for mercy.

after.line: Ten years ago a village like this would have had an angel overhead. Now it has me. Come to Thraben. The Lunarch will want to see anyone who can fight.

hero.half: Cast a spell. Keep them human.

battles.title: The Blood of Stensia
battles.blurb: Mikaeus, the Lunarch, leads the Church of Avacyn from Thraben. He is taking his cathars into Stensia, where the Voldaren vampires have stopped bothering to hide.

scene.line: The darkness crawls with vampires and ghouls, but we are not without allies.
Never forget our ancestors. They have not forgotten us.
Morbid: some of their cards grow stronger if a creature died this turn. Every cathar who falls feeds them. Do not trade lightly.

villainScene.line: I can make you dance to my tune like a puppet, your very blood eager to obey.
I have seen a hundred mortal families rise and fall. I shall outlast a thousand more.

after.line: Olivia will be back. She always is. Go west, to the Nephalia coast. Our dead are not staying in their graves, and I want to know why.

battles.title: The Stitcher's Workshop
battles.blurb: On the Nephalia coast, the stitcher Geralf builds skaabs out of the dead and sends them up the road. The geist of Saint Traft, a dead cathar who never stopped fighting, haunts the same cliffs.

scene.line: The heron is the symbol of the archangel Avacyn. The fact that such spirits still fly gives the church hope that its founder may one day return.
Undying: when a creature with undying dies with no +1/+1 counter on it, it comes back with one. Kill it twice, or take it away for good.

villainScene.line: The best skaab are more powerful and more beautiful than the sum of their parts.
Three heads, six arms, and some armor grafts are better than . . . the normal numbers of those things.
Let those idiot priests tremble! A new era in unlife begins here and now. Oglor, raise the lightning vane!

after.line: One of the skaabs in Geralf's yard wears the Lunarch's face. Mikaeus is dead, and somebody has raised him.
The church will hide this as long as it can. Find the planeswalkers. They are the only ones on this world who are not afraid.

battles.title: The Veil's Curse
battles.blurb: Two planeswalkers have come to Innistrad, and one is hunting the other. Liliana Vess cursed Garruk with an old veil. The curse is killing him, and he has followed her all the way here.

cards.name: Villagers of Estwald // Howlpack of Estwald

scene.line: Your veil's curse won't stop me, deathmage. I have taken down countless night hunters and this dark plane is not big enough for you to hide.
Rid me of this curse, witch, or die with me.
Discard: she makes us both throw cards away. Play your cards out instead of holding them, and she has nothing to take.

villainScene.line: I've seen corpses prettier than you, beastmage.
I come looking for demons and I find a plane full of angels. I hate angels.
Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create.

after.line: I didn't come here for you, Garruk. There is a demon on this world who owns a piece of me, and he is locked in a silver box. Hunt me later.
Later, then. I will find you.

battles.title: The Moon Sage
battles.blurb: Tamiyo, a soratami scholar from another plane, came to Innistrad to study its moon. She has noticed that the Skirsdag, a cult of demon-worshippers hiding inside the church itself, keeps a calendar too.

scene.line: I'm pleased this world has learned the moon affects more than the tides.
Miracle: if a miracle card is the first card you draw in a turn, you can reveal it and cast it for its miracle cost, which is much cheaper. Watch the top of your deck.

villainScene.line: Thraben's pleas fall on deaf ears. Ours do not.
The demons don't care if we mutter niceties and act out ceremonies. Just kill him.

after.line: Their calendar ends on one night: the night they meant to open the Helvault. Somebody else is already planning to do it first.

battles.title: Insectile Aberration
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers the winter of 2011, when a one-mana blue Human that turned into a flier ruled Standard, and the big green ramp deck that tried to grow past it.

scene.line: Flashback: some spells can be cast a second time from the graveyard for their flashback cost. Snapcaster Mage gives any spell flashback for a turn.

villainScene.line: When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.

battles.title: Graveyard Shift
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers spring 2012: black-red Zombies that came back from the graveyard faster than anyone could put them in it, against white-blue Spirits that flew over them.

scene.line: With Thraben's army recalled to its city walls, outlying villages were left to fend for themselves.
Sacrifice: Blood Artist drains them whenever any creature dies. Your zombies are made to die and come back.

villainScene.line: Mist is the geists' sorrow. Wind is their pain. Fire is their vengeance.

battles.title: Griselbrand
battles.blurb: The Helvault breaks. Avacyn is free, and so is the demon she was holding. Thalia and Tamiyo stand with the angel in the rubble while Griselbrand's cult drags him back to full strength.

scene.line: A golden helix streaked skyward from the Helvault. A thunderous explosion shattered the silver monolith and Avacyn emerged, free from her prison at last.
Avacyn emerged from the broken Helvault, but her freedom came at a price—him.
His cult will put him in the graveyard and pull him back out. Watch the graveyard, and keep an answer for the big one.

villainScene.line: The demon Griselbrand dared to stand against Avacyn, earning him the loathing of thousands and the admiration of a few.
"Oh mighty Griselbrand, Scourge of the Heedless World, gladly I consume myself for thee!"

half.line: Keep him busy. I'm nearly there.

battles.title: Burning Vengeance
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, two decks that played out of the graveyard instead of their hand.

archive.format: Standard: Scars of Mirrodin block, Innistrad and Magic 2012.
archive.what: A blue-red deck that filled its own graveyard with Desperate Ravings, Think Twice and Forbidden Alchemy, then flashed them back with Burning Vengeance on the table so every flashback spell also dealt 2 damage.
archive.why: Innistrad was built around the graveyard, and both of these decks used it as a second hand. The Spider Spawning player mills itself on purpose, then flashes back Spider Spawning for an army.
archive.beat: Race it. Burning Vengeance is slow to set up, and every spell it flashes back is one it already cast. Kill Snapcaster Mage on sight.
archive.after: This tribute uses only this act's sets, so the Magic 2012 cards these decks used, like Ponder and Mana Leak, are not in it.

deck.name: Burning Vengeance
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: Stensian vampires encourage spiders near their manors so they can rob the webs.
Fill your own graveyard. The spiders are already in it.

villainScene.line: Mist is the geists' sorrow. Wind is their pain. Fire is their vengeance.
